key_insight: The paper shows that ultra-high-rate Cornucopia quantum codes can support universal fault-tolerant computation with low overhead by using modular blocks and reusable logical-operation gadgets.
engineering_relevance: This architecture preserves the memory efficiency of high-rate quantum error correction while making individually addressable logical qubits practical for scalable quantum computer design.
method: Use the [[2844,1426,18]] Cornucopia code as a 1,426-logical-qubit module with 2,844 physical qubits.
Connect code blocks with bridges to form a modular computer and exploit translation symmetry to create reusable logical gadgets.
Provide three logical instruction sets: basic, high-throughput, and fixed-extractor, each designed for low overhead.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that, excluding magic-state factories, a module with workspace for the basic instruction set averages 4.1 physical qubits per logical qubit versus 3.0 for memory alone.
watch_item: The reported overhead excludes magic-state factories, so end-to-end system cost may be higher in a full fault-tolerant implementation.
paper_title: A modular quantum computer based on Cornucopia codes
